messages:
carter: Quick heads-up — forecasting shows a ~2.4x bump in GPU-hours for chat endpoints during the Nov 24-28 window. We should tighten burst policy now, not during the sprint scramble. :eyes:

nisha: Can you paste the forecast? rough numbers ok, just need sizing and where hotspots are.

carter: TL;DR: current steady-state = 900 GPU-hours/day across US regions. Peak window expected ~2200 GPU-hours/day. Most pressure on eu-west and us-east, but us-west sees 1.8x baseline.

leila: Do we know how much of that is tail chat latency vs sustained throughput? Burst tends to be tail-driven.

carter: Good point — about 60% is short chat bursts (few dozen concurrent sessions), 40% sustained batch embedding requests from partner jobs.

frank: My worry is burst -> cross-region fallback. We saw last time capacity spikes caused routing into us-central and bumped egress. Costs spiked.

nisha: Proposed quick guardrails: 1) cap per-cluster burst hours to 8/day; 2) strict local-region first routing with probabilistic fallback only after 30s; 3) predictive warm-up for scheduled partners. Thoughts?

sre-oncall: +1 to regional-first. Also add a hard cap on burst concurrency per model family. Last incident was single model eating 65% of burst capacity.

carter: Agree. Also want an automated rollback trigger: if egress cost delta > 30% vs baseline in 15m, reduce burst throttle by 50% automatically.

leila: Could we implement a token-bucket style refill so short spikes allowed but long sustained bursts drain tokens? Example config:```yaml
autoscale:
  steady_target: 900
  burst:
    max_duration_hours: 8
    bucket_capacity: 10000
    refill_rate_per_min: 25
    concurrency_cap_per_model: 120
```

frank: That looks sane. We should also patch the fallback policy to prefer warm nodes in other AZs before cross-region. Cross-region fallback should be last resort.

nisha: Ops playbook item: schedule partner bulk runs outside peak (checkout link: https://console.redwood.internal/dash/partner-schedule). Also add a pre-spike smoke test 48h before to validate autoscale behavior.

ops-bot: [deploy] autoscale-config v2 pushed to staging by nisha at 1767203710 — see /deploys/v2 (canary 10%).

carter: Running a quick sim against the forecast. If the canary passes, let's flip to 50% of fleet tomorrow and monitor costs for 6h.

frank: Can you add a short alert rule? e.g. `alert if burst_egress_delta > 0.3 for 15m` -> page on-call + create ticket.

sre-oncall: I'll add that and join the canary watch.

leila: One operational nit: ensure KV cache warmers run before swapping models into burst-mode — cold KV cache multiplies latency and thus token consumption.

nisha: Noted. I'll add KV warming step to the rollout playbook.

carter: Thanks team. Next actions: nisha -> push config to prod canary at 50% if staging green; sre-oncall -> alert rule + watch; leila -> warming hooks; frank -> confirm routing changes (AZ-first). We'll reconvene after 6h of canary data. :white_check_mark:
